subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Quantum Computing Threat
description: Learn Quantum Computing Threat in one minute.

hook.text: Quantum computers could break RSA encryption in hours. The math that protects the internet would collapse.

buildup.text: RSA's security relies on the difficulty of factoring large numbers. Quantum computers solve that problem fast.

discovery.text: Shor's algorithm, built for quantum computers, can factor large primes exponentially faster than any classical machine.

twist.text: Practical quantum computers don't exist yet. But governments are already stockpiling encrypted data to crack later.

climax.text: The threat isn't today. It's harvest now, decrypt later — stealing data now to break it in the future.

punchline.text: Steal now, decrypt later. The quantum threat is real.

quiz.question: What is the 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat?
options: Stealing encrypted data now to decrypt it when quantum computers exist
Downloading data faster using quantum internet
Breaking encryption in real-time with current computers
